findings.rule: AC-002 robustness: no silent loss of a declared release class (round-1 warning only partly fixed)
findings.evidence: Three declaration shapes are still neither bound nor reported, so validate returns [] and require_progression(..., 'ship') returns READY with no proof (probed in temp projects): (1) a class inside a step heading, '### Step 1 — Sign **Evidence class:** release' (heading() never runs the _UNBOUND_CLASS check, the text just becomes part of the title); (2) a class written as a heading, '#### **Evidence class:** release' under a step; (3) '__Evidence class:__ release' on a numbered item in numbered-item mode (line 116: the item branch is taken, _INLINE_CLASS only knows '**', and the elif _UNBOUND_CLASS check is skipped). execution-rules.md:59 claims validate rejects '`__Evidence class:__`'.
findings.correction: Run the _UNBOUND_CLASS check on heading text (in heading(), on the title outside inline code) and on the numbered-item text when _INLINE_CLASS found nothing. Add these three shapes to test_invalid_evidence_classes_are_reported and to test_ship_fails_closed_on_an_invalid_plan.

findings.rule: AC-002 robustness: an announced proof must not satisfy the ship gate
findings.evidence: Placeholder detection only rejects a bare emoji or a cell whose first word is pending/tbd/todo/not yet/missing/... . These cells count as proofs (recorded_release_proofs probe), and '⏳ Pending notarization' lets ship pass in a temp project: '⏳ Pending release', '❌ Not produced', '(pending)', 'none yet', 'blocked', '?', 'will be produced at release'. LiveSpec tables mark status with ✅/❌/⏳ (implementation.md uses '✅ Pass'), so an emoji-prefixed pending cell is a likely way to write it. execution-rules.md:62 says a cell that only announces a proof is not one.
findings.correction: Strip leading status emoji and punctuation ('⏳', '❌', '(', '[') before the _PROOF_PENDING match, add 'none', 'blocked' and '?' to it, and add these cells to test_announced_or_example_proof_keeps_release_pending. Alternatively, require the proof cell to name a path or receipt identifier.

findings.rule: Robustness against hostile input (round-1 regex warning: _CLASS fixed, a new super-linear pattern remains)
findings.evidence: _HEADING = r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$' backtracks cubically on a heading with a long run of spaces followed by a character. Measured: '### Step ' + N spaces + 'x' takes 0.10 s for N=500, 0.76 s for N=1000 and 5.9 s for N=2000; N=8000 did not finish in 20 s. The same holds for '# x' + spaces + '#'*N + 'y'. The pattern runs on every plan validate, every spec-implement or spec-feature goal render, every ship progression, and on implementation.md. Honest documents never contain this, but the fix summary says the regexes no longer backtrack quadratically.
findings.correction: Match '^(#{1,6})(?:\s+(.*))?$' and strip the closing '#' sequence and whitespace in Python (rstrip, then rstrip('#'), then rstrip). Add a timing guard test with a 10k-space heading.

findings.evidence: In numbered-item mode every top-level numbered item of the section opens a step. A numbered intro list before the 'Step' headings, or a second numbered list (risks, notes) inside the same section, restarts at 1. With a classified step this produces 'Step 1 appears 2 times' (probe: '1. prereq / 2. prereq2 / ### Step 1 — Sign + release'). It fails closed and the message is clear, but the plan is valid.
findings.correction: Optional: stop numbered-item steps at the first Step heading (drop the items read before it), or document that a plan with a release step must not hold another top-level numbered list in its Implementation Plan section.

findings.evidence: 'Each step names the evidence it produces and its class' reads as a mandatory class line on every step, while spec-plan SKILL.md:313 says 'local (default, omit it)' and the parser defaults to local.
findings.correction: Say 'Each step names the evidence it produces; a step whose proof needs release signing, a device fleet or production adds **Evidence class:** release (local is the default and is omitted).'

findings.evidence: runtime_context.pending_release_evidence is hashed into goal_hash. Writing a plan with a release step during /spec-feature, or recording a proof in implementation.md, recompiles the goal. goal_recompile carries forward still-valid evidence and only resets the outcome task. The same pattern already exists for delivery_lane. Not a blocker.
findings.correction: None required; optionally mention it in the changelog.

findings.evidence: PROMPT_VERSION stays '2' by design (identity hashes exclude prompts), so current plan reviews stay valid. Side effect: a review prepared before 090 counts as current although its reviewer never saw the minimal-scope rule, and the longer plan prompt can change batch packing near --review-max-chars.
findings.correction: None required; already recorded in implementation.md Decisions.
